summary: gcd returns the greatest common divisor of its integer arguments as a nonnegative integer.
documentation: gcd returns the greatest common divisor of its integer arguments as a nonnegative integer. Zeros and negative inputs are supported; all-zero inputs return zero, and calling it without arguments also returns zero.
caution: A greatest common divisor is not the least common multiple. Zero has special identity behavior, so retain it rather than dividing by the result without a separate guard.
scenarios: Find a common whole-unit package size dividing several stock counts.
Reduce an integer fraction by its common divisor.
Find a shared grid unit for several integer dimensions.
title: Find a common integer divisor
problem: Return math.gcd(*input). Support negative integers and zeros. An empty list and an all-zero list both return zero.
hint: Import gcd and unpack the list into its arguments.
goal: Use math.gcd() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
